before: Bare continuation and ``process this document'' are separate declared prompt conditions. Model~P retains its defining Core/protocol prompt in its prompt-only condition; removing that prompt is a separate comparison, not silently the same P treatment. A study using these measures as a retention score must freeze the combination in advance and continue to report every component, so increased identity signature cannot conceal intrusion or missed stakes.
after: Report bare continuation and ``process this document'' separately. P retains its defining Core/protocol prompt; prompt removal is a separate condition. Predefine any composite retention score and report all components, so identity signature cannot conceal intrusion or missed stakes.

before:
These theater variants remove
different information; a study must choose and declare one or report them as
separate arms rather than pool them into an unspecified control.
after:
These theater variants remove different information; declare one or report

before:
H2's Teacher-generation claim is unsupported at the tested scale if graph
memory does not improve the preregistered artifact outcomes over rolling prose
where structured long-range state should matter. A Teacher benefit without
Student transfer supports the former result but not the transfer extension;
a rating gain that disappears on independent outcome checks is a weaker result
than useful trace improvement. Report generation quality, Student transfer,
and live deployment separately, with poisoning, ossification, latency, and
audit costs beside each. The full chain remains the stronger goal, while a
break in one link does not erase a demonstrated benefit at another.
after:
H2's Teacher-generation claim depends on useful artifact gains over rolling
prose where structured state should matter, including independent outcome
checks rather than ratings alone. A Teacher benefit without Student transfer
supports generation but not the transfer extension. Report generation,
transfer, and live deployment separately, with poisoning, ossification,
latency, and audit costs: the full chain is the stronger goal, but a break in
one link does not erase a benefit at another.

before:
The study must declare which earlier source spans or states the Student itself
has encountered, what remains in its context, and the token distance of a
callback. Without that information, a hit and a phantom may be indistinguishable
to a model denied the record; the transferable target is then a well-chosen
check and warranted restraint, not impossible recall.
after:
Declare the Student's earlier source exposure, retained context, and callback
distance. If hit and phantom are indistinguishable without the record, the
transfer target is a well-chosen check and warranted restraint, not impossible
recall.

before:
If query theater
matches the genuine graph under a sensitive, adequately powered comparison,
this test does not distinguish persistent structure from the performance of
checking; it does not alone prove that either Student learned only style. If
rolling prose matches it, the graph has not earned its added structure on this
endpoint. Report useful task completion and answerability beside abstention,
so neither universal querying nor universal refusal to remember can win by
default.
after:
Parity with query theater would not distinguish persistent structure from
performed checking, but would not prove style-only learning. Parity with
rolling prose means the graph has not earned its structure on this endpoint.
Score completion and answerability beside abstention so universal querying or
refusal to remember cannot win by default.

before:

matched-evidence comparator can further ask whether typed graph structure adds
value beyond external evidence, without replacing the core K--B deployment
contrast.
after:
Declare the model-only fallback under matched inference conditions. An
additional source-retrieval comparator can distinguish graph-specific value
from the benefit of external evidence.

before:

    independent evidence makes an injection detectable, and report harder
    internally consistent poisoning separately rather than assuming every

after:
Distinguish detectably conflicting injections from internally consistent
    poisoning that available evidence may not expose.

before:
Score supported-answer accuracy, unsupported-memory and
poisoning-induced error, calibrated abstention, latency, and useful completion
under preregistered tradeoffs; no single rate should reward blind trust or
universal abstention.
after:
Report supported-answer accuracy, poisoning-induced error, abstention,
latency, and useful completion together.

before:
Each study should declare which memory benefit it presupposes rather
than requiring every earlier branch to succeed.
after: Prerequisites depend on the regime being tested.

before:
This changes graph handles and operations as well as
their rendering; a frozen field-level description and matched source/token
budgets should make those differences explicit. Evaluate both formats under
the same deployment condition, with live graph access a separate factor.
Narrower field ablations can then locate any advantage within the full regime
contrast.

If Model~G matches Model~B on coherence and usefulness at lower measured cost
under the same no-harness condition, implicit training may be preferable for
that model-only use. If B outperforms G under matched access, the explicit
representation has earned a benefit in that comparison; further ablations must
identify whether handles, operations, topology, or rendering explain it. Such
an advantage does not establish that explicit queries are necessary for all
robust long-range reasoning. The stronger possibility that explicit operations
enable capabilities prose does not reliably teach remains a hypothesis, to be
tested across tasks and deployment configurations.
after:
If G matches B on coherence and usefulness at lower cost without a harness,
implicit training may be preferable for that use. A B advantage at matched
access supports the explicit format in that comparison, not universal query
necessity. Whether explicit operations enable capabilities prose does not
reliably teach remains a stronger hypothesis for cross-task and deployment
tests.

before:
Declare whether the comparison fixes total
training budget or per-source exposure, since aligned layers repeat some
content and add target tokens. Preserve that alignment as the treatment while
using layer and alignment ablations to distinguish cross-layer learning from
extra exposure.
after:
Declare the budget/source normalization: aligned layers add tokens and
repeat content. Layer and alignment ablations distinguish cross-layer learning
from extra exposure.

before:
Report graph-mode gains or losses separately, preserving the stronger
joint prose-and-graph criterion above. The Understanding Graph may still be
useful during annotation or in explicit graph modes; a null prose-transfer
result does not erase those benefits. Compare measured costs and uncertainty
before concluding that the unified regime has not earned its additional
training burden in the tested setting.
after:
Report graph-mode results and costs separately against the stronger joint
criterion above. A null prose-transfer result leaves possible annotation and
explicit-graph benefits intact; it limits the demonstrated value of unified
training in this setting.

before:

to succeed first.
after: Each study depends on its relevant branch.

after:
Report packing, repetition, optimizer schedule, and checkpoints; retention
and learning dynamics caused by order remain outcomes.

before: Report effect sizes, uncertainty, early-era retention, and measured serialization cost rather than treating nonsignificance alone as proof of equivalence. If the comparison precisely rules out the declared worthwhile benefit, Tier~(a) is the supported simpler choice for that setting; other scales or schedules remain separate hypotheses.
after: Use the shared uncertainty convention, early-era retention, and measured serialization cost. If a worthwhile benefit is precisely ruled out, Tier~(a) is the supported simpler choice in that setting.

before: The study should declare auxiliary-update and budget controls that distinguish the forecast--commitment--reveal--correction loop from extra supervised examples, feedback, or compute, without equalizing away the loop itself.
after: Auxiliary-update and budget controls should distinguish the forecast--commitment--reveal--correction loop from extra examples, feedback, or compute.

before:

after:
For the user study, declare tasks, participants, and reliance measures;

before: Both are empirical optimization questions for the relevant successful branches: mixture studies depend on useful regime signals, while era granularity depends on the interactive temporal mechanism. They remain part of the integrated architecture's longer-term optimization without requiring every branch to pass before either can be investigated.
after: Both optimize the integrated architecture, with branch-specific prerequisites: useful regime signals for mixtures and a useful interactive temporal mechanism for era granularity.
